what_happened: Dispatch's premise pre-verification held up under independent re-derivation: the harvest-and-widen merge in update-task-status.sh is real and additive, and exactly one live call site (skill_postflight_update in skill-base.sh) reaches it -- orchestrator-postflight.sh's parallel Stage 7 branch is confirmed dead code via its own header comment. This let research converge quickly on recommending dispatch option (a) (a single stderr notice at the two update_state_json() merge points, gated on the post-merge delta rather than the raw forwarded list) without needing to re-litigate the originating change request's framing.

Planning found that test-update-task-status.sh's existing Case 11 sub-cases already produce exactly the three delta scenarios the notice needs (11a delta-2 on the real-write branch, 11b delta-0 cry-wolf, 11c delta-1 on the status-noop branch), each already redirecting stderr to its own log, and test-skill-base-lifecycle.sh Group 4a already captures the live plan-postflight stderr while merging two new paths. The test phase therefore needs zero new fixtures -- four grep assertions against logs that already exist.

A repo-wide sweep for command-substitution or 2>&1 captures of update-task-status.sh found zero hits (skill-base.sh invokes it as a bare statement capturing only $?), which independently retires the 'a new stderr line could be mistaken for parsed output' risk the research report left open and let the plan commit to option (a) without a stdout/stderr compatibility phase.

update-phase-status.sh corrupted the Phase 1 heading when setting IN_PROGRESS: the phase name contains a backtick-wrapped bracket literal `[file-scope]` and the script's bracket-matching apparently matched that inner bracket instead of the trailing [NOT STARTED] marker, truncating the heading to '### Phase 1: Emit the delta-gated `[IN PROGRESS]' and discarding the rest of the title plus the original status bracket. Manually repaired the heading text via Edit to restore the full title with [IN PROGRESS]. Root cause not fixed (out of this dispatch's scope); future plans with a bracket literal in a phase title may hit the same corruption.

Plan Phase 1/2 verification text names 'bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only test-update-task-status.sh' (the deployed path). In this deploy-consumer repo, verify-deploy.sh's own Gate 8 unconditionally SKIPS run-all.sh when invoked from the deployed tree ('is a deploy consumer, not the source store -- run-all.sh does not apply', verify-deploy.sh line ~576) -- it only runs the core extension's shell suites when TARGET is the source store itself. Running the deployed-path invocation directly also fails for an unrelated reason: test-update-task-status.sh's own SOURCE_STORE_SCRIPTS override resolves to $REPO_ROOT/agent-system/extensions/core/scripts, which does not exist inside this repo (the real source store is the external path /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core). The correct invocation, matching Gate 8's own resolution, is from the source store: 'cd /home/benjamin/.config/nvim && bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only test-update-task-status.sh'. Ran it from there; suite passes with all pre-existing Case 11 assertions green.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/update-task-status.sh' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

While verifying Phase 2 via the source-store's own full gate set (cd /home/benjamin/.config/nvim && bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh), found two failures unrelated to this task's edits: (1) doc-lint (check-extension-docs.sh) reports 'script referenced in docs/skills/agents but NOT in provides.scripts: check-evidence-probes.sh' for the core extension -- no occurrence of that script name anywhere in this task's edits; (2) the full shell-suite run (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh, 136 suites) reports one unrelated failure, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh (14 passed, 1 failed), about orchestrator eager-load budget ceilings, not file_scope. Confirmed both pre-existing/unrelated by direct inspection; neither references update-task-status.sh, test-update-task-status.sh, or test-skill-base-lifecycle.sh. A transient third failure (manifest-driven content-hash drift on test-skill-base-lifecycle.sh) was self-caused by editing the source file while a background redeploy was in flight from an earlier timestamp; a second redeploy after finishing the edit cleared it. The two suites this phase actually touches both pass cleanly, confirmed both via --only targeting and via the full 136-suite run.
